description: Open a composition version as the generated React or Vue code actually running in a browser (a single screen mounted by the preview host with generated sample records, or a workflow app): an existing compositionId (and optional version) or an object and context composed now as a new composition. Generates one or both frameworks onto the version, seeds the deterministic field model, compiles each artifact once through the preview host and returns one URL per framework with the lineage (compositionId, version, parentVersion, operation, head), the schema hash and the compiled module digests; the page leads with the running app under its brand, theme and width controls, with the lineage and the measurements one toggle below it, and brand and theme re-mount the app in place. Measurements are stored on the version and the result's measured block names them: the code.generate validation receipt per framework, artifact.certify for every placed chart, and axe-core run inside the running page per framework, brand and theme; every measurement not taken is listed under notMeasured, so nothing is claimed that did not run. The HTTP bridge hosts the preview in-process and the stdio adapter starts it on 127.0.0.1 for Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Cursor, so the extracted runtime bundle serves it with no Vite, npm install or browser automation. A client that negotiates the MCP Apps extension (io.modelcontextprotocol/ui) with the stdio adapter also receives the preview app as a ui:// resource: the same running app with its lineage and measurements, the brand, theme, framework and width switches, the four edits, compare side by side, accept and request changes, inside the conversation. The MCP Apps SDK reference host v1.7.5 rendered React and Vue inside the conversation with OODS_MCP_APPS_UI=1 through a local HTTP-to-stdio relay and a fixed-file serving adjustment for the hidden checkout. Its initialize request advertises no UI capability, so the default is a text result; no Claude Desktop or Cursor run is recorded. action compare (compositionId@version against another version) returns the structural what-changed the compare page shows: regions added, removed or reordered, slot components, nodes outside slots, props, field order, the seed and artifact files whose hash moved, with the side-by-side URL; identical versions report zero differences. action edit applies one operation to compositionId@version by re-composing through the override surface and re-generating, and records the result as a new version with its parent and the operation, then opens it: reorder-region (regionOrder), swap-slot (slot, component from the composer's own candidates), reorder-fields (region, fieldOrder), seed (seed); the parent version is never changed, and an operation that names nothing on the version or changes nothing is refused with OODS-V204. action versions lists the composition's versions with their lineage. The render result's editable block names the regions, slots with candidates, field order and seed an edit may use; the page offers the same four edits. Typed limits: without a reachable host (a native server run on its own, a host reading another schema store root, or a platform without a bundled esbuild binary) the outcome is OODS-N021, retryable, with the host details in data; an unknown composition or version is OODS-N022. Mapped team packages resolve from an installed folder or an absolute mapping localPath, must match their exact version pin, and are bundled with OODS Foundry globals preserved. Package content hashes bind the stored artifacts; opening latest after a package changes records a new version, while an explicit old version serves frozen ESM and MCP-app modules. Missing or unbuildable packages fail with OODS-V217. Package scripts are never installed or run; imported CSS must inline its assets. Writes only the version's artifacts, model, package identity and compiled module snapshots; never saves or edits a schema. A running preview is an observation, not usability certification. Context beside the design: pass contextItems with the decisions and evidence YOU already fetched about this object — each carrying source, id, title, body or excerpt, the query that produced it and when you fetched it — and OODS Foundry validates them, keys them to the composition object and its OODS Foundry URN (urn:oods:object:<Name>@<version>), stores them on the version beside the measurements so they travel with the lineage, and renders them beside the running app on both surfaces. OODS Foundry opens no database, store or network connection belonging to CMOS, TraceLab or Hive and never will: a direct reader would couple the portable bundle to another product schema. An item naming an object the composition does not show is refused with OODS-V207 and nothing is written; a malformed item is refused with OODS-V206. Pass contextSearched for a source that returned nothing, so an empty panel states what was searched rather than leaving the reader unable to tell nothing-found from nobody-asked. An edit carries the panel onto the new version and marks every item, because it was gathered for the design as it was before. Observation beside the design: pass observationRunPath, a Stage1 run directory on this machine, and OODS Foundry reads its identity_graph and object_rollup through structuredData.fetch, compares them with this version's own schema for the object on screen, and shows the rows beside the running app on both surfaces — observed-only, composed-only, agreeing and disagreeing, each disagreement naming its axis (entity, input, data-bound), every row naming the Stage1 run, target, artifact and capture time beside the OODS Foundry object, context and URN. The rows are evidence a person judges: nothing is proposed, applied or queued, and OODS Foundry opens no other product's store or writes into the run. OODS-V208 refuses a path that is not one Stage1 run, OODS-V209 an artifact outside the accepted schema_version, OODS-V210 a composition whose object the registry does not hold; each writes nothing. An edit carries the rows onto the new version and marks every one. Run view: pass runPath, a Stage1 run directory on this machine, with object Run, Finding or CapturedArtifact, and the version shows that run's REAL records — the run, its findings with their result state and provenance, its attested artifacts — read only through structuredData.fetch's run-view kinds; OODS Foundry never calls Stage1 or writes into the run. OODS-V212 refuses a path that is not one Stage1 run, OODS-V213 an artifact outside the admitted contract, OODS-V214 a composition that is not a capture object or a version already showing a different capture identity or manifest; each writes nothing. Nothing is proposed, applied or queued. Capture inspection in the browser appUrl: use presentation stage1-inspection to omit the accessibility score and show measurement limits. Run/Violations/Needs review/Artifacts navigation is read-only, filters and keyboard row opening work, and evidence links recheck the selected operand against the pinned capture manifest and SHA-256. Pass recordId with a fresh runPath detail/card/inline request to select an exact record; unknown IDs are refused before compose. Existing versions retain their record and presentation; a different capture ID or changed manifest is refused even for the same target. These navigation controls live in the browser appUrl, not the inline conversation renderer. Derived Comparison: pass analysisPath (separate from runPath) with object Comparison or ComparisonSignal. Summary, filtered signal list and exact recordId detail use generated React/Vue. Signal detail requires its analysis-id#/signals/N recordId. Both comparands retain paths, JSON pointers and SHA-256; cached navigation and every evidence open recheck all pinned retained bytes. Source and analysis identities/times stay distinct; copied inputs are not rerun. Synthetic zero is labelled; typeface comparands remain incomplete, with no type conformance ratio or source accessibility score. These read-only controls are in browser appUrl; human acceptance and public distribution are separate. Mapped team component contract reports are stored on the preview version and shown in Measurements. Unmet obligations are warnings; unmeasured obligations remain explicitly not-checked. Stored chart artifacts record the token CSS build that drew them. Reopening through design.preview regenerates stale charts; a browser page opened from the saved version flags a token build change until redrawn.

inputSchema.description: Open a composition version as the generated React or Vue app actually running in a browser: either an existing compositionId (and optional version) or an object and context composed now as a new composition. The preview host (in the HTTP bridge, or started by the stdio adapter) compiles the artifact and serves it at one URL per version with its lineage and brand, theme and width controls. action "compare" returns the structural what-changed between this version and `against` (regions, slots, nodes, props, field order, seed, artifact file hashes) with the side-by-side URL. action "accept" records the version as the composition's accepted version with a snapshot of its measurements.

action.description: render (default): open the version as the running app. compare: the what-changed between compositionId@version and against. edit: apply one operation to compositionId@version by re-composing through the override surface and re-generating, recording a new version with its parent, then open it. versions: list the composition's versions and the accepted one. accept: record compositionId@version (default its latest) in the composition's accepted.json with when, the OODS Foundry head, the schema hash and a snapshot of the version's measurements; a later accept supersedes it with lineage, and a version not generated yet or already the accepted one is refused with OODS-V205.

against.description: action compare: the version on the right; the left is compositionId@version.

compositionId.description: The other composition; default the same composition.

analysisPath.description: Portable Stage1 derived-analysis directory. Composes Comparison or ComparisonSignal from attested retained bytes, separate from runPath. Only read-only contexts; recordId selects an exact signal.

compositionId.description: An existing composition from design.compose; with no version, its latest version opens.

context.description: View context for object-aware composition. Determines which view_extensions are applied. When object is provided without layout, context infers the layout (detail→detail, list→list, form→form). workflow assembles list/detail/form/timeline screens with trait actions, routes, four UI states and generated application data.

contextItems.description: Decisions and evidence about this object that YOU already fetched, shown beside the running preview and stored on the version. OODS Foundry opens no database, store or network connection belonging to CMOS, TraceLab or Hive and never will: a direct reader would couple the portable bundle to another product's schema. Every item must carry its own provenance — source, id, title, the query that produced it and when you fetched it — because OODS Foundry cannot re-run your search to check it. An item naming a different object from the one on screen is refused with OODS-V207 and nothing is written; a malformed item is refused with OODS-V206.

body.description: What it says, in full. Supply this or excerpt.

excerpt.description: Your own shortening of it; OODS Foundry never shortens content itself.

fetchedAt.description: When you fetched it, ISO-8601. Items fetched before this version was composed are marked on the panel rather than hidden.

id.description: Its identifier in that source, so a reader can go and find it.

object.description: The object it is about; must be the composition's object.

query.description: The query that produced it. Without this the panel cannot say why the item is here.

source.description: Where it came from, as your own tool names it: cmos.decisions, tracelab.evidence, hive.person.

timestamp.description: The time the item itself carries — when the decision was taken, not when you fetched it.

urn.description: Alternatively its OODS Foundry URN, urn:oods:object:<Name>@<version>.

contextSearched.description: What you searched that returned nothing, so an empty panel is a statement rather than a silence: the reader can tell 'nothing was found' from 'nobody asked'.

edit.description: action edit: the one operation to apply to compositionId@version. The parent version is never changed.

component.description: swap-slot: one of the composer's own candidates for that slot on the parent version (the version record lists them).

fieldOrder.description: reorder-fields: the region's field names in the desired order.

regionOrder.description: reorder-region: the screen's region ids in the desired order (the version record lists them).

framework.description: Which generated app to compile and serve; both frameworks by default, each at its own URL.

object.description: Object name from the OODS registry (e.g., 'Subscription', 'User'); with context, composes a new composition (version 1) and opens it.

observationRunPath.description: A Stage1 run directory on this machine (out/stage1/<suite>/<run-uuid>). OODS Foundry reads its identity_graph and object_rollup through structuredData.fetch, compares them with this version's own schema for the object on screen, and stores the rows beside the running app on both surfaces: observed-only, composed-only, agreeing and disagreeing, each disagreement naming its axis (entity, input, data-bound), and every row naming the Stage1 run, target, artifact and capture time beside the OODS Foundry object, context and URN. The rows are evidence a person judges; nothing is proposed, applied or queued. OODS Foundry opens no other product's store and writes nothing into the run. A path that is not one Stage1 run is refused with OODS-V208, an artifact outside the accepted schema_version with OODS-V209, and a composition whose object the registry does not hold with OODS-V210; each refusal writes nothing. An edit carries the rows onto the new version and marks every one, because they compared the design as it was.

brand.description: Brand the page mounts with (data-brand and the matching token CSS scope).

fieldGroups.description: Number of field groups for form layout.

metricColumns.description: Number of metric columns for dashboard layout.

tabCount.description: Number of tabs for detail layout.

tabLabels.description: Custom tab labels for detail layout.

theme.description: Theme the page mounts with (data-theme and the matching token CSS scope).

presentation.description: Named Stage1 inspection presentation: omit the accessibility score and prominently show measurement limits. Source records remain unchanged.

recordId.description: Exact record ID for a fresh runPath or analysisPath detail/card/inline view. Unknown IDs refuse before composition; existing versions retain their selected record.

runPath.description: A Stage1 run directory on this machine (out/stage1/<suite>/<run-uuid>) whose REAL records this version shows: the run itself for Run, its findings for Finding, its attested artifacts for CapturedArtifact. OODS Foundry reads the run only through structuredData.fetch's admitted run-view kinds (run_manifest, a11y_report 2.2.0/2.3.0, report_index 1.0.0/1.1.0, a11y_evidence 1.1.0/1.2.0), every file under the run manifest's sha256 attestation, and never calls Stage1 or writes into the run. A path that is not one Stage1 run is refused with OODS-V212, an artifact outside the admitted contract with OODS-V213, and a composition that is not Run, Finding or CapturedArtifact, or a version already showing a different capture identity or manifest, with OODS-V214; each refusal writes nothing. Nothing is proposed, applied or queued: a person reads the run view.

version.description: The version of compositionId to open.
